title: Definition
body_md:
We define $Hol(D)$ to be the space of functions $f: D \to \mathbb C$ such that 
    \[
        \frac{\partial f}{\partial z^*} = 0. 
    \]

title: Definition
body_md:
For $0 < p < \infty$, we define $H^p(D)$ to be the space of functions $f \in Hol(D)$ such that 
    \[
        ||f||_{H^p} := \sup_{0 < r < 1} \left( \int_0^{2\pi} |f(re^{i\theta})|^p \,d\theta \right)^{1/p} < \infty.
    \]
head: environment

label: bvcon
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{bvcon}
A function $f \in H^p(D)$, $0 < p < \infty$, has nontangential boundary values $f_{nt} \in L^p(\partial D)$ at almost every point of $\partial D$, 
\[
\lim_{r\nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} |f(re^{i\theta})|^p \, d\theta = \int_0^{2\pi} |f_{nt}(e^{i\theta})|^p \,d\theta,
\]
and
\[
\lim_{r\nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} |f(re^{i\theta})- f_{nt}(e^{i\theta})|^p \, d\theta = 0.
\]
head: environment

label: bvcircle
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{bvcircle}Let $f: D \to \mathbb C$. We say that $f$ has a boundary value in the sense of distributions, denoted by $f_b \in \mathcal{D}'(\partial D)$, if, for every $\varphi \in C^\infty(\partial D)$, the limit
            \[
             \langle f_b, \varphi \rangle := \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} f(re^{i\theta}) \, \varphi(\theta) \,d\theta
            \]
            exists.
head: environment

label: GHJH23point1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{GHJH23point1}
For $f \in Hol(D)$, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For every $\phi \in C^\infty(\partial D)$, there exists the limit
    \[
             \langle f_b, \phi \rangle := \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} f(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta.
            \]

    \item There is a distribution $f_b \in \mathcal{D}'(\partial D)$ such that $f$ is the Poisson integral of $f_b$
    \[
             f(re^{i\theta}) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\langle f_b, P_r(\theta - \cdot) \rangle,
            \]
    where 
    \[
        P_r(\theta) = \frac{1-r^2}{1-2r\cos(\theta) +r^2}
    \]
    is the Poisson kernel on $D$. 

    \item There are constants $C>0$, $\alpha \geq 0$, such that 
    \[
        |f(re^{i\theta})| \leq \frac{C}{(1-r)^\alpha},
    \]
    for $0 \leq r < 1$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Definition

\label{vekopondisk}
For $f: D \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z  \in \mathbb{C}$, we denote by $T(\cdot)$ the integral operator defined by 
\[
T(f)(z) = -\frac{1}{\pi} \iint_D \frac{f(\zeta)}{\zeta - z}\, d\xi\,d\eta,
\]
whenever the integral is defined.

label: VekKlimThmcombined
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{VekKlimThmcombined}
For $f \in L^1(D)$, 
\[
    \frac{\partial}{\partial z^*} T(f) = f.
\]
If $f \in L^q(D)$, $1 \leq q \leq 2$, then $T(f) \in L^\gamma(D)$, where $1 < \gamma < \frac{2q}{2-q}$, $T(f)|_{\partial D(0,r)} \in L^\mu(\partial D(0,r))$, 
\[
||Tf||_{L^\mu(\partial D(0,r))} \leq C ||f||_{L^q(D)},
\]
$0 < r \leq 1$, and 
\[
\lim_{r\nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} |T(f)(e^{i\theta}) - T(f)(re^{i\theta})|^\mu \,d\theta = 0, 
\]
where $\mu$ satisfies $1 < \mu < \frac{q}{2-q}$ and $C$ is a constant that does not depend on $r$ or $f$. For $f \in L^q(D)$, $q > 2$, $T(f) \in C^{0,\alpha}(\overline{D})$, with $\alpha = \frac{ q-2}{q}$.

title: Definition
body_md:
For $0 < p < \infty$, we define the bicomplex Lebesgue space $L^p(D, \mathbb{B})$ to be the set of functions $f: D \to \mathbb{B}$ such that 
    \[  
        ||f||_{L^p(D,\mathbb{B})}:= \left( \iint_D ||f(z)||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \,dx\,dy \right)^{1/p} < \infty.
    \]
    Similarly, we define $L^p(\partial D, \mathbb{B})$ to be the set of functions $g: \partial D \to \mathbb C$ such that 
    \[
        ||g||_{L^p(\partial D,\mathbb{B})}:= \left( \int_{\partial D} ||g(z)||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \,d\sigma(z) \right)^{1/p} < \infty,
    \]
    where $\sigma$ is Lebesgue surface measure on $\partial D$.

title: Theorem

title: Theorem
body_md:

\[
||T_\mathbb{B}(f)||_{L^\gamma(\partial D(0,r),\mathbb{B})} \leq C ||f||_{L^q(D,\mathbb{B})},
\]
where $C$ is a constant that does not depend on $r$ or $f$, and
\[
\lim_{r\nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||T_\mathbb{B}(f)(e^{i\theta}) - T_\mathbb{B}(f)(re^{i\theta})||_\mathbb{B}^\gamma \,d\theta = 0, 
\]
for $1 \leq \gamma < \frac{q}{2-q}$. For $f \in L^q(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q > 2$, $T(f) \in C^{0,\alpha}(\overline{D},\mathbb{B})$, with $\alpha = \frac{ q-2}{q}$.

label: complexVekua
title: Definition
body_md:
For $0 < p < \infty$ and $A, B : D\to\mathbb{C}$, we define the Vekua-Hardy spaces $H^p_{A,B}(D)$ to be the collection of $w: D \to \mathbb{C}$ such that 
    \begin{equation}\label{complexVekua}
    \frac{\partial w}{\partial z^*} = Aw + Bw^*
\end{equation}
and 
\[
    \sup_{0 < r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} |w(re^{i\theta})|^p \,d\theta < \infty.
\]
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Functions that solve (\ref{complexVekua}) are called generalized analytic functions by those who follow the works of Vekua \cite{Vek} and are called pseudoanalytic functions (or pseudoholomorphic functions) by those who follow the works of Bers \cite{Bers}. For a specific pair of coefficients $A$ and $B$, we denote by $H_{A,B}(D)$ the collection of solutions of (\ref{complexVekua}). The Vekua-Hardy spaces (and their higher-order variations) have been previously considered in, for example, \cite{KlimBook, PozHardy, CompOp, moreVekHardy, conjbel,threedvek, WB3, WBD}.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{bcbdinsfuncins}
Let $p$ be a positive real number. Every $f \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$ such that $f_{nt} \in L^s(\partial D, \mathbb{B})$, where $s > p$, is an element of $H^s(D,\mathbb{B})$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem \ref{thm: bchardyrep}, if $f \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$, then $(f^+)^*, f^- \in H^p(D)$. By Theorem \ref{propLqiff}, since $f_{nt} \in L^s(\partial D,\mathbb{B})$, it follows that $f^\pm_{nt} \in L^s(\partial D)$. Since 
\[
    |(f^+)^*(z)| = |f^+(z)|
\]
for all $z \in D$, it follows that $(f^+)^*_{nt}, f^-_{nt} \in L^s(\partial D)$. By Theorem \ref{VekHardyCombined} statement (3), $(f^+)^*,f^- \in H^s(D)$. Therefore, by Theorem \ref{thm: bchardyrep}, $f \in H^s(D,\mathbb{B})$.

label: bcGHJH23point1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{bcGHJH23point1}
For $f \in Hol(D,\mathbb{B})$, the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
         \item For every $\phi \in C^\infty(\partial D)$, there exists the limit
    \[
             \langle f_b, \phi \rangle := \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} f(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta.
            \]

    \item There is a distribution $f_b = p^+ f_b^+ + p^- f^-_b \in \mathcal{D}'(\partial D)$ such that $f$ is representable as
    \[
             f(re^{i\theta}) = p^+\left(\frac{1}{2\pi}\langle (f^+_b)^*, P_r(\theta - \cdot) \rangle \right)^* + p^-\frac{1}{2\pi}\langle f^-_b, P_r(\theta - \cdot) \rangle,
            \]
    where 
    \[
        P_r(\theta) = \frac{1-r^2}{1-2r\cos(\theta) +r^2}
    \]
    is the Poisson kernel on $D$. 

    \item There are constants $C>0$, $\alpha \geq 0$, such that 
    \[
        ||f(re^{i\theta})||_\mathbb{B} \leq \frac{C}{(1-r)^\alpha},
    \]
    for $0 \leq r < 1$.
    \end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose there exists constants $C>0$, $\alpha \geq 0$, such that 
    \[
        ||f(re^{i\theta})||_\mathbb{B} \leq \frac{C}{(1-r)^\alpha},
    \]
    for $0 \leq r < 1$. So, by \eqref{stareqn},
    \begin{align*}
        |f^\pm(re^{i\theta})| \leq \sqrt{2}||f(re^{i\theta})||_\mathbb{B} \leq  \frac{\sqrt{2}C}{(1-r)^\alpha}.
    \end{align*}
    for all $0 \leq r < 1$. Since $f \in Hol(D,\mathbb{B})$, it follows by Theorem \ref{thm: bchardyrep} that $(f^+)^*,f^- \in Hol(D)$. Since $|(f^+)^*(re^{i\theta})| = |f^+(re^{i\theta})|$, for all $re^{i\theta}$, it follows, by Theorem \ref{GHJH23point1}, that $(f^+)^*_b, f^-_b$ exist. Since
    \[
       \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} (f^+)^*(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta = \left(\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} f^+(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta ,\right)^*
    \]
    for $\phi \in C^\infty(\partial D,\mathbb{R})$, it follows that $f^+_b$ exists. Thus, for every $\phi \in C^\infty(\partial D)$, 
    \[
\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} f(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta = p^+\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} f^+(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta + p^-\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} f^-(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta ,
    \]
    and the sum of limits on the right hand exists. Hence, $f_b$ exists.

    Suppose $f_b$ exists. Since, for every $\phi \in C^\infty(\partial D)$, we have
    \[
         \int_0^{2\pi} f(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta = p^+ \int_0^{2\pi} f^+(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta + p^-\int_0^{2\pi} f^-(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta, 
    \]
    for every $r$, and
    \[
        \left|\int_0^{2\pi} f^\pm(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta \right| \leq \sqrt{2} \left|\left|\int_0^{2\pi} f(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta \right|\right|_\mathbb{B},
    \]
    for every $r$, it follows that 
    \[
    \left|\lim_{r\nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} f^\pm(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta \right| \leq \sqrt{2} \left|\left|\lim_{r \nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} f(re^{i\theta}) \, \phi(\theta) \,d\theta \right|\right|_\mathbb{B},
    \]
    and the limit on the right hand side exists. Thus, $f^\pm_b$ exist. By similar reasoning as above, $(f^+)^*_b$ exists. Since $(f^+)^*, f^- \in Hol(D)$, it follows, by Theorem \ref{GHJH23point1}, that 
    \[
        (f^+)^*(re^{i\theta}) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \langle (f^+)^*_b, P_r(\theta - \cdot) \rangle
    \]
    and 
    \[
        f^-(re^{i\theta}) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \langle f^-_b, P_r(\theta - \cdot) \rangle.
    \]
    Since $f= p^+ f^+ + p^- f^-$, it follows that
    \begin{align*}
        f(re^{i\theta}) = p^+\left( \frac{1}{2\pi} \langle (f^+)^*_b, P_r(\theta - \cdot) \rangle\right)^* + p^- \frac{1}{2\pi} \langle f^-_b, P_r(\theta - \cdot) \rangle.
    \end{align*}

    Finally, suppose that 
    \[
f(re^{i\theta}) = p^+\left( \frac{1}{2\pi} \langle (f^+)^*_b, P_r(\theta - \cdot) \rangle\right)^* + p^- \frac{1}{2\pi} \langle f^-_b, P_r(\theta - \cdot) \rangle.
    \]
    Since $(f^+)^*, f^- \in Hol(D)$ and are representable as distributional pairings against the Poisson integral, it follows, by Theorem \ref{GHJH23point1}, that there exist constants $C_\pm > 0$ and $\alpha_\pm \geq 0$ such that 
    \[
        |(f^+)^*(re^{i\theta})| \leq \frac{C_+}{(1-r)^{\alpha_+}}
    \]
    for every $re^{i\theta} \in D$, 
    and
    \[
|f^-(re^{i\theta})| \leq \frac{C_-}{(1-r)^{\alpha_-}},
    \]
    for every $re^{i\theta} \in D$. Thus, 
    \begin{align*}
        ||f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}} 
        &\leq 2^{-1/2}\left( |f^+(re^{i\theta})| + |f^-(re^{i\theta})|\right) \\
        &=2^{-1/2}\left( |(f^+)^*(re^{i\theta})| + |f^-(re^{i\theta})|\right) \\
        &\leq 2^{-1/2}\left( \frac{C_+}{(1-r)^{\alpha_+}} + \frac{C_-}{(1-r)^{\alpha_-}}\right)\\
        &\leq \frac{C}{(1-r)^\alpha},
    \end{align*}
    where $C:= 2\max\{2^{-1/2}C_+, 2^{-1/2}C_-\}$ and $\alpha := \max\{\alpha_+, \alpha_-\}$, for every $re^{i\theta} \in D$.

\label{bcvekhardyrepgeneral}
    Let $0 < p < \infty$. For every $f \in H_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ such that $\bar\partial f= Af + B\overline{f} \in L^q(D, \mathbb{B})$, $q>2$, with representation $f = \varphi + T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})$, $ f \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ if and only if $\varphi \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$. The result holds when $1 < q \leq 2$ so long as $p$ satisfies $p < \frac{q}{2-q}$.
head: environment

label: returnpoitbcvekhardy
title: Proof
body_md:
By hypothesis, $\bar\partial f= Af + B\overline{f} \in L^1(D, \mathbb{B})$, so by Proposition \ref{Prop: bcrepsecond}, 
\[
        f = \varphi + T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f}).
\]
Suppose that $\varphi \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$. Then, for $r \in (0,1)$, we have
\begin{align}
 \int_0^{2\pi} ||f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta 
 &= \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta}) + T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \nonumber \\ 
 &\leq C_p\left( \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p + \int_0^{2\pi} ||T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \right) \nonumber\\
  &\leq C_p\left( ||\varphi||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p + \int_0^{2\pi} ||T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \right), \label{returnpoitbcvekhardy}
\end{align}
where $C_p$ is a constant that depends on only $p$. By Theorem \ref{bctbehavior}, since $ Af+B\overline{f}\in L^q(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q>2$, it follows that $T_\mathbb{B}(Af+B\overline{f}) \in C^{0,\alpha}(\overline{D},\mathbb{B})$. Thus, there exists $M>0$ such that 
\[
        ||T_\mathbb{B}(Af+B\overline{f})(z)||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \leq M,
\]
for every $z \in \overline{D}$. Hence, 
\begin{align*}
C_p\left( ||\varphi||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p + \int_0^{2\pi} ||T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \right)
&\leq C_p\left( ||\varphi||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p + 2\pi M \right)< \infty.
\end{align*}
Since there is no dependence on $r$ in the right hand side of the above inequality, we have 
\begin{align*}
||f||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p &\leq C_p\left( ||\varphi||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p + 2\pi M \right)< \infty.
\end{align*}
If $1 < q \leq 2$ and $p$ satisfies $p < \frac{q}{2-q}$, then returning to (\ref{returnpoitbcvekhardy}) we have
\begin{align*}
C_p\left( ||\varphi||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p + \int_0^{2\pi} ||T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \right)
&\leq C_p\left( ||\varphi||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p + C||T_\mathbb{B}(Af+B\overline{f})||^p_{L^q(D)} \,d\theta \right) < \infty,
\end{align*}
by Theorem \ref{bctbehavior}. Since the right hand side has no dependence on $r$, we have
\[
||f||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p \leq C_p\left( ||\varphi||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p + C||T_\mathbb{B}(Af+B\overline{f})||^p_{L^q(D)} \,d\theta \right) < \infty.
\]
In either case $f \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$. 

Now, suppose that $f = \varphi + T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f}) \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$. Observe that, for $r \in (0,1)$, we have
\begin{align}
    \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})||_\mathbb{B}^p \,d\theta 
    &= \int_0^{2\pi} ||f(re^{i\theta}) - T_\mathbb{B}(Af+B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta})||_\mathbb{B}^p \,d\theta \nonumber \\
    &\leq C_p \left( \int_0^{2\pi} ||f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta + \int_0^{2\pi} || T_\mathbb{B}(Af+B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta})||_\mathbb{B}^p \,d\theta\right)  \label{returnpointagain}\\
    &\leq C_p\left( ||f||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p + M 2\pi\right)< \infty,\nonumber
\end{align}
where $C_p$ is a constant that depends on only $p$ and $M$ is a constant that bounds $||T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(z)||_\mathbb{B}^p$, for all $z \in \overline{D}$. So, 
\[
||\varphi||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p \leq C_p\left( ||f||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p + M 2\pi\right)< \infty,
\]
and $\varphi \in H^p(D, \mathbb{B})$. If $1 < q \leq 2$ and $p$ satisfies $p < \frac{q}{2-q}$, then returning to (\ref{returnpointagain}) and appealing to Theorem \ref{bctbehavior} once more, we have 
\begin{align*}
&C_p \left( \int_0^{2\pi} ||f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta + \int_0^{2\pi} || T_\mathbb{B}(Af+B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta})||_\mathbb{B}^p \,d\theta\right) \\
&\leq C_p \left( \int_0^{2\pi} ||f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta + C||T_\mathbb{B}(Af+B\overline{f})||^p_{L^q(D)}\right)  < \infty.
\end{align*}
Therefore, 
\[
    ||\varphi||^p_{H^p_\mathbb{B}} \leq C_p \left( \int_0^{2\pi} ||f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta + C||T_\mathbb{B}(Af+B\overline{f})||^p_{L^q(D)}\right)  < \infty,
\]
and $\varphi \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$.

label: thm: bcvekbzerorep
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: bcvekbzerorep}
Let $A \in L^1(D, \mathbb{B})$. Every $f \in H_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ is representable as 
\[
    f(z) = \varphi(z)e^{\phi(z)},
\]
where $\varphi \in Hol(D,\mathbb{B})$ and 
$
    \phi(z) = T_\mathbb{B}(A)(z)$.
In the case that $A \in L^q(D,\mathbb{B})$, where $q>2$, $T_\mathbb{B}(A) \in C^{0,\alpha}(\overline{D},\mathbb{B})$, for $\alpha = \frac{q-2}{q}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The representation is a consequence of Theorem 14 of \cite{FundBicomplex}. See also Remark 38 of \cite{BCBergman}.

The inclusion of $\phi$ in the specified class is a consequence of Theorem \ref{bctbehavior}.
head: environment

label: thm: bcvekhardybzerorep
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: bcvekhardybzerorep}
Let $0 < p < \infty$ and $A \in L^q(D, \mathbb{B})$, $q>2$. For every $f \in H_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $f = \varphi e^\phi\in H^{p}_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ if and only if $\varphi \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that $f  = \varphi e^\phi \in H_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ and $\varphi \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$. Then, for each $r \in (0,1)$, we have
\begin{align*}
    \int_0^{2\pi} ||f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta
    &=\int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
    &\leq 2^{p/2}\int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})||^p_\mathbb{B} \,||e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta.
\end{align*}
Since $e^\phi \in C^{0,\alpha}(\overline{D},\mathbb{B})$, it follows that there exists $M>0$ such that $||e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}||_{\mathbb{B}} < M$, for all $re^{i\theta} \in \overline{D}$. Hence, 
\begin{align*}
2^{p/2}\int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})||^p_\mathbb{B} \,||e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta
&\leq 2^{p/2}M^p\int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})||^p_\mathbb{B}  \,d\theta\\
&\leq 2^{p/2}M^p ||\varphi||^p_{H^p_{\mathbb{B}}} \,d\theta < \infty.
\end{align*}
Thus, 
\[
\sup_{0< r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \leq 2^{p/2}M^p ||\varphi||^p_{H^p_{\mathbb{B}}} \,d\theta < \infty,
\]
and $f \in H^p_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$. 

Now, suppose that $f = \varphi e^\phi \in H^p_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$. Since $\phi \in C^{0,\alpha}(\overline{D},\mathbb{B})$, by Theorem \ref{thm: bcvekbzerorep}, it follows that $(e^\phi)^+, (e^\phi)^- \in C^{0,\alpha}(\overline{D})$, where $e^\phi = p^+ (e^\phi)^+ + p^- (e^\phi)^-$. Since continuous functions on compact sets are bounded, it follows that there exist $M_+,M_-, m_+, m_- > 0$ such that 
\[
    m_+ \leq |(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^+|\leq M_+
\]
and 
\[
    m_- \leq |(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^-|\leq M_-,
\]
for all $re^{i\theta} \in \overline{D}$. Since $e^v$ is not a zero divisor for all $v \in \mathbb{B}$,  it follows that $e^v$ is invertible, for all $v \in\mathbb{B}$, see \cite{FundBicomplex}. Let $m:= \min\{m_+,m_-\}$ and $M:= \max\{M_+,M_-\}$. Then,
\[
m \leq |(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^+|\leq M
\]
and
\[
m \leq |(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^-|\leq M,
\]
for all $re^{i\theta} \in \overline{D}$. Hence, 
\[
\frac{1}{m} \geq \frac{1}{|(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^+|}\geq \frac{1}{M}
\]
and
\[
\frac{1}{m} \geq \frac{1}{|(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^-|}\geq \frac{1}{M},
\]
for all $re^{i\theta} \in \overline{D}$. Thus, for $r \in (0,1)$, we have
\begin{align*}
    \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})||_\mathbb{B}^p \,d\theta
    &= \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})} (e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^{-1}||_\mathbb{B}^p \,d\theta \\
    &\leq 2^{p/2}\int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})} ||_\mathbb{B}^p \,||(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^{-1}||_\mathbb{B}^p \,d\theta \\
    &\leq \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})} ||_\mathbb{B}^p \left( \frac{1}{|(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^+|} + \frac{1}{|(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^-|}\right)^p \,d\theta \\
     &\leq \frac{2^p}{m^p} \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})} ||_\mathbb{B}^p  \,d\theta \\
     &= \frac{2^p}{m^p} \int_0^{2\pi} ||f(re^{i\theta}) ||_\mathbb{B}^p  \,d\theta \\
     &\leq \frac{2^p}{m^p} || f||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p  < \infty.
\end{align*}
Therefore, 
\[
    ||\varphi||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p \leq C ||f||_{H^p_\mathbb{B}}^p < \infty,
\]
where $C$ is a constant that depends only on $p$ and $A$, and $\varphi \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$.
head: environment

label: inBCVekHardypinLebm
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{inBCVekHardypinLebm}
Let $p$ be a positive real number and $A\in L^q(D)$, $q>2$. Every function $w \in H^p_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ is an element of $L^m(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $0 < m < 2p$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem \ref{thm: bcvekhardybzerorep}, if $w \in H^p_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$, then $w = e^\phi \varphi$ and $\varphi \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$. Since $\varphi \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$, it follows, by Proposition \ref{Prop: bchardymlessthan2p}, that $\varphi \in L^m(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $0 < m < 2p$. Since $A \in L^q(D)$, $q>2$, it follows that $e^\phi \in C^{0, \alpha}(\overline{D},\mathbb{B})$. So, there exists a positive real number $M$ such that 
\[
||e^{\phi(z)}||_{\mathbb{B}} < M
\]
for all $z \in \overline{D}$. Hence, 
\begin{align*}
 \iint_D ||w(z)||_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy
 &= \iint_D ||e^{\phi(z)} \varphi(z)||_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy\\
 &\leq 2^{m/2}\iint_D ||e^{\phi(z)}||_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,|| \varphi(z)||_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy\\
 &\leq 2^{m/2}M^m\iint_D  || \varphi(z)||_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy< \infty,
\end{align*}
for every $0 < m < 2p.$ Therefore, $w \in L^m(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $0 < m < 2p$.

title: Theorem

label: bcvekimpliescvek
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{bcvekimpliescvek}
Let $A, B \in L^q(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q>2$. A function $w:D\to\mathbb{B}$ solves
\[
    \bar\partial w = Aw + B\overline{w}
\]
if and only if
\[
    \frac{\partial (w^+)^*}{\partial z^*} = (A^+)^* (w^+)^* + (B^+)^* w^+
\]
and
\[
    \frac{\partial w^-}{\partial z^*} = A^- w^- + B^- (w^-)^*.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Definition \ref{bcdbardef},  
\[
    \bar\partial = p^+ \frac{\partial}{\partial z} + p^- \frac{\partial}{\partial z^*}.
\]
By Proposition \ref{everybchasplusandminus},
\[
    w = p^+ w^+ + p^-w^-,\quad A = p^+ A^+ + p^- A^-, \text{ and } B= p^+ B^+ + p^- B^-,
\]
where $w^\pm, A^\pm, B^\pm : D\to\mathbb{C}$. Observe that 
\begin{align*}
    \bar\partial w &:= \left( p^+ \frac{\partial}{\partial z} + p^- \frac{\partial}{\partial z^*}\right) (p^+w^+ + p^- w^-) = p^+\frac{\partial w^+}{\partial z} + p^- \frac{\partial w^-}{\partial z^*}.
\end{align*}
So, if $w$ solves $\bar\partial w= Aw + B\overline{w}$, then 
\begin{align*}
    &p^+\frac{\partial w^+}{\partial z} + p^- \frac{\partial w^-}{\partial z^*} \\
    &= Aw + B\overline{w} \\
    &= (p^+ A^+ + p^- A^-)(p^+ w^+ + p^-w^-) + (p^+ B^+ + p^- B^-)\overline{(p^+ w^+ + p^-w^-)}\\
    &= (p^+ A^+ + p^- A^-)(p^+ w^+ + p^-w^-) + (p^+ B^+ + p^- B^-)(p^+ (w^+)^* + p^-(w^-)^*)\\
    &= p^+(A^+ w^+ + B^+ (w^+)^*) + p^-(A^- w^- + B^- (w^-)^*).
\end{align*}
Hence, by identifying the components of the idempotent representations on the left and right hand sides, we have
\[
    \frac{\partial w^+}{\partial z} = A^+ w^+ + B^+ (w^+)^*
\]
and
\[
    \frac{\partial w^-}{\partial z^*} = A^- w^- + B^- (w^-)^*.
\]
Since $\frac{\partial w^+}{\partial z} = A^+ w^+ + B^+ (w^+)^*$, it follows that 
\[
    \frac{\partial (w^+)^*}{\partial z^*} = (A^+)^* (w^+)^* + (B^+)^* w^+.
\]
The other direction is clear by reversing the above computation.
head: environment

label: thm: bcvekhardyimpliescvekhardy
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: bcvekhardyimpliescvekhardy}
Let $A, B \in L^q(D, \mathbb{B})$, $q>2$. For $0 < p < \infty$, $w \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ if and only if $(w^+)^* \in H^p_{(A^+)^*,(B^+)^*}(D)$ and $w^- \in H^p_{A^-,B^-}(D)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem \ref{bcvekimpliescvek}, $w \in H_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ if and only if $(w^+)^* \in H_{(A^+)^*,(B^+)^*}(D)$ and $w^- \in H_{A^-,B^-}(D)$. 

Suppose that $w \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$. Since 
\[
    |w^\pm(z)| \leq \sqrt{2}||w(z)||_{\mathbb{B}},
\]
for all $z \in D$, by \eqref{bcbasicestimates}, it follows that 
\[
    \sup_{0< r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} |w^\pm(re^{i\theta})|^p  \,d\theta \leq \sqrt{2} \sup_{0< r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||w(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p  \,d\theta < \infty.
\]
Since $|w^+(z)| = |(w^+)^*(z)|$, for all $z$, it follows that $(w^+)^* \in H^p_{(A^+)^*,(B^+)^*}(D)$ and $w^- \in H^p_{A^-,B^-}(D)$. 

Now, suppose that $(w^+)^* \in H^p_{(A^+)^*,(B^+)^*}(D)$ and $w^- \in H^p_{A^-,B^-}(D)$. Since 
\[
    ||w(z)||_{\mathbb{B}} \leq 2^{-1/2} ( |w^+(z) + w^-(z)|),
\]
for every $z \in D$, by \eqref{bcbasicestimates}, it follows that, for each $re^{i\theta} \in D$, we have
\begin{align*}
    \int_0^{2\pi} ||w(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p  \,d\theta
    &\leq 2^{-p/2}\int_0^{2\pi} |w^+(re^{i\theta})+w^-(re^{i\theta})|^p  \,d\theta \\
    &\leq C_p \left( \int_0^{2\pi} |w^+(re^{i\theta})|^p \,d\theta + \int_0^{2\pi}|w^-(re^{i\theta})|^p  \,d\theta \right)\\
    &\leq C_p \left( \
    \sup_{0< r < 1}\int_0^{2\pi} |w^+(re^{i\theta})|^p \,d\theta + \sup_{0 < r < 1}\int_0^{2\pi}|w^-(re^{i\theta})|^p  \,d\theta \right),
\end{align*}
where $C_p$ is a constant that depends only on $p$. Since the right hand side of the above inequality has no dependce on $r$, it follows that 
\[
\sup_{0 < r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||w(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p  \,d\theta \leq C_p \left( \
    \sup_{0< r < 1}\int_0^{2\pi} |w^+(re^{i\theta})|^p \,d\theta + \sup_{0 < r < 1}\int_0^{2\pi}|w^-(re^{i\theta})|^p  \,d\theta \right) < \infty.
\]
Therefore, $w \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
We end this subsection by recognizing that Casta\~neda and Kravchenko proved, in Theorem 3 of \cite{CastaKrav}, that solutions of the $\mathbb{B}$-Vekua equation
    \[
        \bar\partial w = Aw + B\overline{w},
    \]
    with $B$ neither zero nor a zero divisor, are also representable by a similarity principle representation analogous to solutions of the complex Vekua equation. With this representation, the results for the complex-valued Vekua-Hardy spaces of \cite{KlimBook,PozHardy, CompOp, moreVekHardy, conjbel} should be immediately recoverable. We leave the details to the interested reader.
head: environment

label: thm: bcvekbdinsimprincase
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: bcvekbdinsimprincase}
    For $0 < p < \infty$ and $A \in L^q(D, \mathbb{B})$, $q>2$, every $f = \varphi e^\phi \in H^p_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ such that $\varphi^+ \in H^p_w(D)$, where $\varphi = p^+ \varphi^+ + p^- \varphi^-$ and $w \in L^\gamma(D)$, and $\gamma>2$ or $1< \gamma \leq 2$ and $p$ satisfies $p < \frac{\gamma}{2- \gamma}$, has a nontangential limit $f_{nt} \in L^p(D, \mathbb{B})$, and 
    \[
        \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta  = 0. 
    \]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorems \ref{thm: bcvekbzerorep} and \ref{thm: bcvekhardybzerorep}, if $A \in L^q(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q>2$ and $f \in H^p_{A,0}(D)$, then $f = \varphi e^\phi$ and $\varphi \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$. By Theorem \ref{bcholobvcon}, since we assume that $\varphi^+ \in H^p_w(D)$ and $w$ and $p$ satisfy the relationship that $w \in L^\gamma(D)$ with $\gamma>2$ or $p < \frac{\gamma}{2-\gamma}$, it follows that $\varphi$ has a nontangential boundary value $\varphi_{nt} \in L^p(\partial D,\mathbb{B})$ and 
\[
        \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \varphi(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta  = 0. 
    \]
Since $f = \varphi e^\phi$, $\varphi_{nt}$ exists and is in $L^p(\partial D,\mathbb{B})$, and $e^\phi \in C^{0, \alpha}(\overline{D},\mathbb{B})$ by Theorem \ref{thm: bcvekbzerorep}, it follows that $f_{nt}$ is in $L^p(\partial D,\mathbb{B})$. Also, for $r \in (0,1)$, we have 
\begin{align*}
    &\int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
    &= \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta})e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})} - \varphi(re^{i\theta})e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})} ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
    &= \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta})e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})} -\varphi(re^{i\theta})e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})} + \varphi(re^{i\theta})e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})} - \varphi(re^{i\theta})e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})} ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
    &= \int_0^{2\pi} ||(\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) -\varphi(re^{i\theta}))e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})} + \varphi(re^{i\theta})(e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})} - e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
    &\leq  C_p \left( \int_0^{2\pi} ||(\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) -\varphi(re^{i\theta}))e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})}||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta + \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})(e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})} - e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \right) \\
    &\leq  C_p \left( 2^{p/2}\int_0^{2\pi} ||(\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) -\varphi(re^{i\theta}))||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,||e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})}||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta + \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})(e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})} - e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \right) \\
     &\leq  C_p \left( 2^{p/2}M \int_0^{2\pi} ||(\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) -\varphi(re^{i\theta}))||_{\mathbb{B}}^p  \,d\theta + \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})(e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})} - e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \right),
\end{align*}
where $C_p$ is a constant that depends on only $p$ and $M$ is a constant that depends on only $p$ and $A$. Since
\begin{align*}
    &\varphi(re^{i\theta})(e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})} - e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})\\
    &= p^+[\varphi^+(re^{i\theta}) ((e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})})^+-(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^+)] + p^-[\varphi^-(re^{i\theta}) ((e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})})^- -(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^-)],
\end{align*}
it follows that 
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})(e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})} - e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta\\
&=\int_0^{2\pi} ||p^+[\varphi^+(re^{i\theta}) ((e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})})^+-(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^+)] + p^-[\varphi^-(re^{i\theta}) ((e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})})^- -(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^-)] ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
&\leq 2^{-p/2}  \int_0^{2\pi} |\varphi^+(re^{i\theta}) ((e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})})^+-(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^+)|^p \,d\theta \\
&\quad\quad + 2^{-p/2} \int_0^{2\pi} |\varphi^-(re^{i\theta}) ((e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})})^- -(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^-) |^p \, d\theta .
\end{align*}
So, 
\begin{align*}
&C_p \,\left( 2^{p/2}M \int_0^{2\pi} ||(\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) -\varphi(re^{i\theta}))||_{\mathbb{B}}^p  \,d\theta + \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})(e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})} - e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \right)\\
&\leq C_p \, 2^{p/2}M \int_0^{2\pi} ||(\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) -\varphi(re^{i\theta}))||_{\mathbb{B}}^p  \,d\theta \\
&\quad\quad +  C_p\,  2^{-p/2}  \int_0^{2\pi} |\varphi^+(re^{i\theta}) ((e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})})^+-(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^+)|^p \,d\theta \\
&\quad\quad + C_p \,2^{-p/2} \int_0^{2\pi} |\varphi^-(re^{i\theta}) ((e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})})^- -(e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})})^-) |^p \, d\theta
\end{align*}
Observe that the first integral summand in the right hand side of the above inequality will converge to $0$ as $r \nearrow 1$ by Theorem \ref{bcholobvcon}, and the second and third integral summands in the right hand side of the above inequality will converge to $0$ by Lebesgue's Dominated Convergence Theorem as $r \nearrow 1$. Thus, 
\[
\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta = 0.
\]

label: bcvekhardybdinsfuncins
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{bcvekhardybdinsfuncins}
Let $p$ be a positive real number and $A \in L^q(D)$, $q>2$. Every $f \in H^p_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ such that $f_{nt} \in L^s(\partial D, \mathbb{B})$, where $s > p$, is an element of $H^s_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem \ref{thm: bcvekhardybzerorep}, $f = e^\phi \varphi$, and $\varphi \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$. Since $A \in  L^q(D)$, $q>2$, it follows that $e^\phi \in C^{0, \alpha}(\overline{D},\mathbb{B})$. So, there exist real numbers $m>0$ and $M>0$ such that 
\[
m < ||e^{\phi(z)}||_{\mathbb{B}} < M
\]
for all $z \in \overline{D}$. So, 
\begin{align*}
\int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^s \,d\theta
&= \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\frac{e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})}}{e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})}}\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^s \,d\theta\\
&\leq \frac{2^{s/2}}{m^s} \int_0^{2\pi} ||e^{\phi(e^{i\theta})}\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta})||^s_{\mathbb{B}} \,d\theta\\
&= \frac{2^{s/2}}{m^s} \int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta})||^s_{\mathbb{B}} \,d\theta < \infty
\end{align*}
and $\varphi_{nt} \in L^s(\partial D, \mathbb{B})$. By Theorem \ref{bcbdinsfuncins}, $\varphi \in H^s(D, \mathbb{B})$. By Theorem \ref{thm: bcvekhardybzerorep}, $f \in H^s_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$.

label: Thm: bcvekhardybvcon
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Thm: bcvekhardybvcon}
Let $0 < p < \infty$. Every $f \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ such that $\bar\partial f= Af + B\overline{f} \in L^q(D, \mathbb{B})$, $q>2$, with representation $f = \varphi + T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})$ and $\varphi^+ \in H^p_w(D)$, where $w \in L^\gamma$, $\gamma>2$ or $1 < \gamma\leq 2$ and $p < \frac{\gamma}{2-\gamma}$, has a nontangential boundary value $f_{nt} \in L^p(\partial D)$ and 
\[
\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta = 0
\]
The result holds when $1 < q \leq 2$ so long as $p$ satisfies $p < \frac{q}{2-q}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem \ref{bcvekhardyrepgeneral}, if $f \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ with $\bar\partial f = Af + B\overline{f} \in L^q(D)$, where $q$ and $p$ satisfy the hypothesis, then $f = \varphi + T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})$ and $\varphi \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$. By Theorem \ref{bcholobvcon}, $\varphi$ has a nontangential boundary value $\varphi_{nt} \in L^p(\partial D,\mathbb{B})$ and 
\[
        \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \varphi(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta  = 0. 
    \]
By Theorem \ref{bctbehavior}, if $p$ and $q$ satisfy the hypothesis, then $T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f}) \in L^p(\partial D,\mathbb{B})$ and 
\[
\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(e^{i\theta}) - T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta  = 0.
\]
So, $f_{nt}$ exists and is in $L^p(\partial D,\mathbb{B})$. Also, for $r \in (0,1)$, we have
\begin{align*}
    &\int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
    &= \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) + T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(e^{i\theta}) - (\varphi(re^{i\theta}) + T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta})) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
    &\leq C_p \left( \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \varphi(re^{i\theta})||_\mathbb{B}^p\,d\theta  + \int_0^{2\pi} || T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(e^{i\theta}) - T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta\right) .
\end{align*}
Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
& \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
&\leq \lim_{r \nearrow 1} C_p \left( \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \varphi(re^{i\theta})||_\mathbb{B}^p\,d\theta  + \int_0^{2\pi} || T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(e^{i\theta}) - T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta\right)\\
&\leq  C_p \left( \lim_{r \nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \varphi(re^{i\theta})||_\mathbb{B}^p\,d\theta  + \lim_{r \nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} || T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(e^{i\theta}) - T_\mathbb{B}(Af + B\overline{f})(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta\right)\\
&= 0.
\end{align*}

label: bcvekhardybvfromidempotent
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{bcvekhardybvfromidempotent}
 For $A,B \in L^q(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q>2$, and $0 < p < \infty$, every $w = p^+ w^+ + p^- w^-\in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ such that $w^+ \in H^p_g(D)$, where $g \in L^\ell(D)$, and $\ell >2$ or $1 < \ell \leq 2$ and $p$ satisfies $p < \frac{\ell}{2-\ell}$, has a nontangential limit $w_{nt} \in L^p(\partial D, \mathbb{B})$, and 
    \[
        \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||w_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - w(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta  = 0. 
    \]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $w \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$. By Theorem \ref{thm: bcvekhardyimpliescvekhardy}, $w = p^+w^+ + p^- w^-$, where $(w^+)^* \in H^p_{(A^+)^*,(B^+)^*}(D,\mathbb{B})$ and $w^- \in H^p_{A^-,B^-}(D)$. Suppose also that $w^+ \in H^p_g(D)$, for some $g \in L^\ell(D)$, $\ell > 2$ (or if $1 < \ell \leq 2$, then $p$ satisfies $p < \frac{\ell}{2-\ell}$). By Theorem \ref{thm: nonhomogHpbvcon} and statement (3) of Theorem \ref{VekHardyCombined}, it follows that $w^+$ and $w^-$ have nontangential boundary values $w^+_{nt}$ and $w^-_{nt}$, respectively, $w^+_{nt}, w^-_{nt} \in L^p(\partial D)$, and,
\[
\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} |w^+_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - w^+(re^{i\theta}) |^p \, d\theta  = 0,
\]
and 
\[
\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} |w^-_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - w^-(re^{i\theta}) |^p \, d\theta  = 0.
\]
By linearity, $w_{nt} = p^+ w^+_{nt} + p^- w^-_{nt}$ exists and is in $L^p(\partial D,\mathbb{B})$. Observe that, for each $r \in (0,1)$, 
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^{2\pi} ||w_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - w(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
&= \int_0^{2\pi} ||p^+ w^+_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) + p^- w^-_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - (p^+ w^+(re^{i\theta}) + p^- w^-(re^{i\theta})) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
&= \int_0^{2\pi} ||p^+ (w^+_{nt}(e^{i\theta})-w^+(re^{i\theta})) + p^- (w^-_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - w^-(re^{i\theta})) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
&\leq \int_0^{2\pi} \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|w^+_{nt}(e^{i\theta})-w^+(re^{i\theta})| + |w^-_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - w^-(re^{i\theta}) |)\right)^p \, d\theta \\
&\leq \frac{C_p}{2^{p/2}}\left(\int_0^{2\pi} |w^+_{nt}(e^{i\theta})-w^+(re^{i\theta})|^p \,d\theta + \int_0^{2\pi} |w^-_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - w^-(re^{i\theta}) |^p \, d\theta \right), 
\end{align*}
where $C_p$ is a constant that depends only on $p$. Since 
\[
\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} |w^+_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - w^+(re^{i\theta}) |^p \, d\theta  = 0
\]
and 
\[
\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} |w^-_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - w^-(re^{i\theta}) |^p \, d\theta  = 0,
\]
it follows that 
\[
\lim_{r \nearrow 1}\frac{C_p}{2^{p/2}}\left(\int_0^{2\pi} |w^+_{nt}(e^{i\theta})-w^+(re^{i\theta})|^p \,d\theta + \int_0^{2\pi} |w^-_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - w^-(re^{i\theta}) |^p \, d\theta \right) = 0.
\]
Therefore, 
\[
\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||w_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - w(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta = 0.
\]

title: Theorem
body_md: For $p \geq 1$ and $A, B \in L^q(D)$, $q>2$, $w \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ if and only if $w \in H_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $w_b$ exists, and $w_b \in L^p(\partial D, \mathbb{B})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First, suppose $w \in H_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $w_b$ exists, and $w_b \in L^p(\partial D)$. Since $w_b$ exists and is in $L^p(\partial D,\mathbb{B})$, it follows, by Proposition \ref{propLqiff}, that $w_b^\pm$ exist and $w^\pm \in L^p(\partial D, \mathbb{C})$. Since 
\begin{align*}
\int_0^{2\pi} (w^+(re^{i\theta}))^*\,\phi(\theta) \,d\theta = \left(\int_0^{2\pi} w^+(re^{i\theta})\,\phi(\theta) \,d\theta \right)^*,
\end{align*}
for every real-valued $\phi \in C^\infty(\partial D)$ and $re^{i\theta} \in D$, and $w^+_b$ exists, it follows that $(w^+)^*_b$ exists. By Theorem \ref{thm: bcvekhardyimpliescvekhardy}, $(w^+)^* \in H_{(A^+)^*, (B^+)^*}(D)$ and $w^- \in H_{A^-,B^-}(D)$. Since $(w^+)^* \in H_{(A^+)^*, (B^+)^*}(D)$ and $w^- \in H_{A^-,B^-}(D)$, $(w^+)^*_b$ and $w^-_b$ both exist, and $(w^+)^*_b,w^-_b \in L^p(\partial D)$, it follows by statement (5) of Theorem \ref{VekHardyCombined} that $(w^+)^* \in H^p_{(A^+)^*, (B^+)^*}(D)$ and $w^- \in H^p_{A^-,B^-}(D)$. By Theorem \ref{thm: bcvekhardyimpliescvekhardy}, $w \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$. 

Now, suppose $w \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$. By Theorem \ref{thm: bcvekhardyimpliescvekhardy}, $(w^+)^* \in H^p_{(A^+)^*, (B^+)^*}(D)$ and $w^- \in H^p_{A^-,B^-}(D)$. By statement (3) of Theorem \ref{VekHardyCombined}, the nontangential boundary values $(w^+)^*_{nt}$ and $w^-_{nt}$ exist and are in $L^p(\partial D)$. By statement (4) of Theorem \ref{VekHardyCombined},  $(w^+)^*, w^- \in L^1(D)$. By part (3) of Theorem \ref{VekHardyCombined} again, 
\[
\lim_{r\nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} |(w^+)^*(re^{i\theta}) - (w^+)^*_{nt}(e^{i\theta})|^p \,d\theta = 0
\]
and
\[
\lim_{r\nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} |w^-(re^{i\theta}) - w^-_{nt}(e^{i\theta})|^p \,d\theta = 0.
\]
By Theorem \ref{lonedistbv}, since $(w^+)^*, w^- \in L^1(D)$, $(w^+)^*_{nt}, w^-_{nt} \in L^p(\partial D) \subset L^1(\partial D)$, and 
\[
\lim_{r\nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} |(w^+)^*(re^{i\theta}) - (w^+)^*_{nt}(e^{i\theta})| \,d\theta = 0
\]
and
\[
\lim_{r\nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} |w^-(re^{i\theta}) - w^-_{nt}(e^{i\theta})| \,d\theta = 0.
\]
it follows that $(w^+)^*_{b}$ and $w^-_{b}$ exist. Also, by Theorem \ref{lonedistbv} $(w^+)^*_{nt} = (w^+)^*_{b}$ and $w^-_{nt} = w^-_{b}$.

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $A \in L^q(D, \mathbb{B})$, $q>2$, and $w \in H_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$. The $\mathbb{B}$-holomorphic factor $\varphi$ (appearing in the representation $w = \varphi e^\phi$ provided by Theorem \ref{thm: bcvekbzerorep}) has a boundary value in the sense of distributions $\varphi_b$ if and only if there exist constants $C>0$ and $\alpha \geq 0$ such that 
\[
    ||w(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}} \leq \frac{C}{(1-r)^\alpha},
\]
for all $re^{i\theta} \in D$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem \ref{thm: bcvekbzerorep}, every $w \in H_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$, where $A \in L^1(D)$, has a representation 
\[
    w = \varphi e^\phi,
\]
where $\varphi \in Hol(D,\mathbb{B})$ and, if $q>2$, $\phi \in C^{0, \alpha}(\overline{D},\mathbb{B}) \subset L^\infty(\overline{D},\mathbb{B})$. 

Suppose $\varphi_b$ exists. By Theorem \ref{bcGHJH23point1}, there exists $C> 0$ and $\alpha \geq 0$ such that 
\[
        ||\varphi(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}} \leq \frac{C}{(1-r)^\alpha},
\]
for all $re^{i\theta} \in D$. Observe that 
\begin{align*}
    ||w(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}} 
    &= ||\varphi(re^{i\theta}) e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}||_{\mathbb{B}} \\
    &\leq \sqrt{2}||\varphi(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}\,||e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}||_{\mathbb{B}}\\
    &\leq \sqrt{2}||\varphi(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}\,||e^{\phi}||_{L^\infty}\\
    &\leq \sqrt{2}\,||e^{\phi}||_{L^\infty}\,\frac{C}{(1-r)^\alpha},
\end{align*}
for every $re^{i\theta} \in D$. Letting $\widetilde{C}:= C\sqrt{2}\,||e^{\phi}||_{L^\infty}$, we have
\[
||w(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}  \leq \frac{\widetilde{C}}{(1-r)^\alpha}
\]
for every $re^{i\theta} \in D$.

Now, assume there are constants $C>0$ and $\alpha \geq 0$ such that 
\[
||w(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}  \leq \frac{C}{(1-r)^\alpha}
\]
for every $re^{i\theta} \in D$. Since $e^\phi \in C^{0,\alpha}(\overline{D},\mathbb{B})$ and $e^\phi$ is neither zero nor a zero divisor, it follows that $\left|\left|\frac{1}{e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}}\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}$ is bounded, i.e., there exists $N>0$ such that
\[
    \left|\left|\frac{1}{e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}}\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}} < N,
\]
for all $re^{i\theta} \in D$. Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
||\varphi(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}} 
&= \left|\left|\frac{w(re^{i\theta})}{e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}}\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}} \\
&\leq \sqrt{2}\,\left|\left|\frac{1}{e^{\phi(re^{i\theta})}}\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}\, ||w(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}} \\
&\leq \sqrt{2}\,N\, ||w(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}\\
&\leq \sqrt{2}\,N\, \frac{C}{(1-r)^\alpha},
\end{align*}
for every $re^{i\theta} \in D$. By Theorem \ref{bcGHJH23point1}, $\varphi_b$ exists.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. We define the bicomplex polyanalytic functions $P^n(D,\mathbb{B})$ to be the set of functions $f: D \to\mathbb{B}$ such that 
    \[
        \bar\partial^n f = 0. 
    \]
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $0 < p < \infty$ and $n$ be a positive integer. We define the bicomplex polyanalytic Hardy spaces $P^{n,p}(D,\mathbb{B})$ to be the set of functions $f \in P^n(D,\mathbb{B})$ such that 
    \[
        \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}||\bar\partial^k f||_{H^p_{\mathbb{B}}} < \infty. 
    \]
head: environment

label: bcpolyrep
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{bcpolyrep}
    Let $n$ be a positive integer. Every $f \in P^{n}(D,\mathbb{B})$ is representable as 
    \[
        f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k,
    \]
    where $\varphi_k \in Hol(D,\mathbb{B})$, for each $k$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Observe that functions of the form $f(z) = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k(z)$, where $\varphi_k \in Hol(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$, are elements of $P^n(D,\mathbb{B})$ by direct computation. 

We prove the other direction by induction. The result is clear for $n = 1$. Suppose that, for every $n$ satisfying $1 \leq n \leq m-1$, that if $f \in P^n(D, \mathbb{B})$, then there exists a collection $\{\varphi_k\}_{k=0}^{n-1}$ such that $\varphi_k\in Hol(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$, and
\[
    f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k
\]
Let $g \in P^m(D, \mathbb{B})$. So, $\bar\partial g \in P^{m-1}(D, \mathbb{B})$, and there exists a collection $\{\varphi_k\}_{k=0}^{m-2}$ such that $\varphi_k \in Hol(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$, and 
\[
    \bar\partial g = \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k.
\]
Observe that 
\begin{align*}
    \bar\partial\left( g - \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}\widehat{z^*} ^{k+1} \varphi_k\right)  
    &= \bar\partial g - \bar\partial \left( \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}\widehat{z^*} ^{k+1} \varphi_k\right) \\
    &= \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k - \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k = 0.
\end{align*}
Thus, $g - \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}\widehat{z^*} ^{k+1} \varphi_k \in Hol(D,\mathbb{B})$. Let 
\[
\gamma = g - \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}\widehat{z^*} ^{k+1} \varphi_k.
\]
Let $\phi_0 := \gamma$ and $\phi_{k+1} := \frac{1}{k+1} \varphi_k$, for every $0 \leq k \leq m-2$. Then we rearrange to have
\[
    g = \sum_{j = 0}^{m-1} \widehat{z^*}^j \phi_j.
\]

label: thm: polyhardyrep
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: polyhardyrep}
    Let $0 < p < \infty$ and $n$ be a positive integer. A function $f$ is in $P^{n,p}(D,\mathbb{B})$ with representation 
    \[
        f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k
    \]
    if and only if $\varphi_k  \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$, for each $k$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that $\{\varphi_k\}_{k=0}^{n-1}\subset H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$. Then 
\[
    f = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\widehat{z^*}^k\varphi_k
\]
solves
\[
    \frac{\partial^n f}{\partial\bar z^n} = 0,
\]
and, for each $r \in (0,1)$,  
\begin{align*}
    \int_0^{2\pi} ||f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta 
    &= \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
    &\leq C\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
    &\leq C\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}2^{p/2}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k\right|\right|_\mathbb{B}^p\left|\left|\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
    &\leq C \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}2^{p/2}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta < \infty,
\end{align*}
where $C$ is a constant that depends on only $p$ and $n$. Thus, 
\[
 \sup_{0 < r < 1}\int_0^{2\pi} ||f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \leq  C \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}2^{p/2}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta < \infty,
\]
and $f \in P^{n,p}(D, \mathbb{B})$. 

Now, suppose that $f \in P^{n,p}(D,\mathbb{B})$. By Theorem \ref{bcpolyrep}, it follows that there exist $\varphi_k \in Hol(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$, such that 
\[
    f = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\widehat{z^*}^k\varphi_k.
\]  
Observe that the explicit form of $\varphi_k$ can be given by 
\begin{align*}
    \varphi_k(z) = \dfrac{1}{k!}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k}\dfrac{(-1)^j}{j!}\widehat{z^*}^j\, \bar\partial^{k+j}f, 
\end{align*}
for each $k$ (see \cite{l2poly} or \cite{itvek, itvekbvp, WBD} for the motivation for this formula in the complex setting). Hence, for each $k$ and $r \in (0,1)$, we have
\begin{align*}
\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta
&= \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\dfrac{1}{k!}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k}\dfrac{(-1)^j}{j!}\widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^j\, \bar\partial^{k+j}f(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \\
&\leq C_p \sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\bar\partial^{k+j}f(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
&\leq C_p \sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k}\sup_{0 < r < 1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\bar\partial^{k+j}f(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta,
\end{align*}
where $C_p$ is a constant that depends on only $p$ and $n$. Since $f \in P^{n,p}(D, \mathbb{B})$, it follows that 
\[
\sup_{0 < r < 1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\bar\partial^{\ell}f(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta < \infty,
\]
for all $\ell$ satisfying $0 \leq \ell \leq n-1$. Thus, 
\[
C_p \sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k}\sup_{0 < r < 1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\bar\partial^{k+j}f(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta < \infty,
\]
so
\[
\sup_{0 < r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi}\left|\left|\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \leq C_p \sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k}\sup_{0 < r < 1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\bar\partial^{k+j}f(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta < \infty.
\]
Therefore, $\varphi_k \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$.

title: Proposition
body_md: For $0 < p < \infty$ and $n$ a positive integer, every $f \in P^{n,p}(D,\mathbb{B})$ is an element of $L^m(D,\mathbb{B})$, for all $0 < m < 2p$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem \ref{thm: polyhardyrep}, every $f \in P^{n,p}(D,\mathbb{B})$ is representable as $f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k f_k$, where $f_k \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$. Since $f_k \in H^p(D,\mathbb{B})$, it follows by Proposition \ref{Prop: bchardymlessthan2p} that $f_k \in L^m(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $0 < m < 2p$. Observe that 
 \begin{align*}
    \iint_D ||f(z)||_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy 
    &= \iint_D \left|\left|\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k f_k(z)\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy \\
    &\leq C\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}\iint_D \left|\left|  f_k(z)\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy < \infty,
 \end{align*}
 where $C$ is a constant that depends on $n$ and $m$. Thus, $f \in L^m(D,\mathbb{B})$.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
For $n$ a positive integer, $0 < p < \infty$, and $w_k \in L^{q_k}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $0 \leq k \leq n-1$, such that $p$ and $q_k$ satisfy $q_k>2$ or $1 < q_k \leq 2$ and $p < \frac{q_k}{2-q_k}$, for all $k$, every $f \in P^{n,p}(D,\mathbb{B})$ with representation
    \[
            f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k
    \]
    such that $\varphi_k^+ \in H^p_{w_k}(D)$, for each $k$, has a nontangential limit $f_{nt} \in L^p(\partial D, \mathbb{B})$, and 
    \[
        \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta  = 0. 
    \]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $\varphi_k^+ \in H^p_{w_k}(D)$ and $w_k \in L^{q_k}(D)$, where $q_k>2$ or $1 < q_k \leq 2$ and $p < \frac{q_k}{2-q_k}$, then, by Theorem \ref{bcholobvcon}, $\varphi_k$ has a nontangential boundary value $\varphi_{k,nt} \in L^p(\partial D, \mathbb{B})$ and 
\[
    \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \varphi_k(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta = 0.
\]
Since each $\varphi_k$ has a nontangential boundary value $\varphi_{k,nt}$ and $f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k$, it follows that $f_{nt}$ exists and is 
\[
    f_{nt} = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_{k,nt}.
\]
Observe that 
\begin{align*}
    \int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p\,d\theta
    &= \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p\,d\theta\\
    &\leq \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} C_p \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p\,d\theta \\
    &\leq \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} C_p \, 2^{p/2}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left| \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p\,d\theta < \infty,
\end{align*}
where $C_p$ is a constant that depends on only $p$ and $n$. Hence, $f_{nt} \in L^p(\partial D, \mathbb{B})$. Now, for $r \in (0,1)$, we have
\begin{align*}
    &\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left| f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \\
    &= \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left| \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) \right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
    &\leq C_p \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left| \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) \right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
    &\quad\quad +  C_p\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left| \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_{k}(re^{i\theta}) - \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) \right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \\
    &= C_p \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|  \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k (\varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) -  \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) )\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
    &\quad\quad +  C_p\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|  (\widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k - \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k )\varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) \right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \\
    &\leq C_p \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|  \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) -  \varphi_k(re^{i\theta} )\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta +  C_p\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|  (\widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k - \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k )\varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) \right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta,
\end{align*}
where $C_p$ is a constant that depends only on $p$ and is not necessarily the same from line to line. Observe that, for every $k$, 
\begin{align*}
(\widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k - \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k )\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})
&= (1-r)^k e^{-jk\theta} (p^+ \varphi_k^+(re^{i\theta}) + p^- \varphi_k^-(re^{i\theta}))
\end{align*}
By Lebesgue's Dominated Convergence Theorem, 
\begin{align*}
&\lim_{r \nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|  (\widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k - \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k )\varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) \right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \\
&= \lim_{r \nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left| (1-r)^k e^{-jk\theta} (p^+ \varphi_k^+(re^{i\theta}) + p^- \varphi_k^-(re^{i\theta})) \right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
&\leq C_{p,k} \left( \lim_{r \nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} | (1-r)^{k} |^p\, | \varphi_k^+(re^{i\theta})|^p \,d\theta + \lim_{r \nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} | (1-r)^{k} |^p\,|\varphi_k^-(re^{i\theta})) |^p \,d\theta\right) = 0,
\end{align*}
for every $k$. Since 
\[
\lim_{r \nearrow 1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|  \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) -  \varphi_k(re^{i\theta} )\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta = 0,
\]
for every $k$, by Theorem \ref{bcholobvcon}, and 
\[
 \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|  (\widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k - \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k )\varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) \right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta = 0,
\]
where $C_{p,k}$ is a constant that depends on only $p$ and $k$, for every $k$, it follows that 
\begin{align*}
&\lim_{r \nearrow 1} C_p\left[ \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|  \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) -  \varphi_k(re^{i\theta} )\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta +  \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}\int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|  (\widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k - \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k )\varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) \right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \right]\\
&= 0.
\end{align*}
Thus, 
\[
\lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left| f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta = 0.
\]

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $0 < p < \infty$, $n$ a positive integer, and $A,B:D \to \mathbb{B}$. We define the class of bicomplex-HOIV (\textit{higher-order iterated Vekua}) functions $V^n_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ to be those functions $f: D \to \mathbb{B}$ that solve the bicomplex HOIV-equation
    \[
        (\bar\partial - A- BC(\cdot))^n f = 0,
    \]
    where $C(\cdot)$ is the operator that applies bicomplex conjugation.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $0 < p < \infty$, $n$ a positive integer, and $A,B \in W^{n-1,q}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q>2$. We define the class of bicomplex HOIV-Hardy functions $V^{n,p}_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ to be those functions $f \in V^n_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ such that 
    \[
        \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} ||(\bar\partial - A- BC(\cdot))^k f||_{H^p_{\mathbb{B}}} < \infty.
    \]
head: environment

label: Thm: bcmetarep
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Thm: bcmetarep}
    Let $n$ be a positive integer and $A \in W^{n-1,q}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q>2$. Every $f \in V^{n}_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ is representable as 
    \[
        f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k,
    \]
    where $\varphi_k \in H_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$, for each $k$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Observe that functions of the form $f(z) = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k(z)$, where $\varphi_k \in H_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$, are elements of $V^n_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ by direct computation. 

We prove the other direction by induction. The result is clear for $n = 1$. Suppose that, for every $n$ satisfying $1 \leq n \leq m-1$, that if $f \in V^n_{A,0}(D, \mathbb{B})$, then there exists a collection $\{\varphi_k\}_{k=0}^{n-1}$ such that $\varphi_k\in H_{A,0}(D,
\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$, and
\[
    f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k
\]
Let $g \in V^m_{A,0}(D, \mathbb{B})$. So, $(\bar\partial-A) g \in V^{m-1}_{A,0}(D, \mathbb{B})$, and there exists a collection $\{\varphi_k\}_{k=0}^{m-2}$ such that $\varphi_k \in H_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$, and 
\[
    (\bar\partial-A) g = \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k.
\]
Observe that 
\begin{align*}
    &(\bar\partial-A)\left( g - \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}\widehat{z^*} ^{k+1} \varphi_k\right) \\  
    &= \left(\bar\partial -A\right)g - \bar\partial \left( \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}\widehat{z^*} ^{k+1} \varphi_k\right) + A  \left( \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}\widehat{z^*} ^{k+1} \varphi_k\right)\\
    &= \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k - \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k  - \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}\widehat{z^*} ^{k+1} A\varphi_k +    \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}\widehat{z^*} ^{k+1} A\varphi_k \\
    &= 0.
\end{align*}
Thus, $g - \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}\widehat{z^*} ^{k+1} \varphi_k \in H_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$. Let 
\[
\gamma = g - \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}\widehat{z^*} ^{k+1} \varphi_k.
\]
Let $\phi_0 := \gamma$ and $\phi_{k+1} := \frac{1}{k+1} \varphi_k$, for every $0 \leq k \leq m-2$. Then we rearrange to have
\[
    g = \sum_{j = 0}^{m-1} \widehat{z^*}^j \phi_j.
\]
head: environment

label: Thm: bcmetahardyrep
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Thm: bcmetahardyrep}
         For $0 < p < \infty$, $n$ a positive integer, and $A \in W^{n-1, q}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q>2$, a function $f$ is in $V^{n,p}_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ with representation 
        \[
            f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k
        \]
        if and only if $\varphi_k \in H^p_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First, suppose that $f \in V^{n,p}_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$. By Theorem \ref{Thm: bcmetarep}, there exists $\varphi_{k} \in H_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ such that
    \[
        f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k.
    \]
    Observe that 
    \[
        \varphi_k = \frac{1}{k!}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k} \frac{(-1)^{j}}{j!} \widehat{z^*}^j (\bar\partial - A)^{k+j}f,
    \]
    for every $k$. For this formula in the complex setting, see Remark 3.2 of \cite{WBD} (or Theorem 1 of \cite{itvek} or Theorem 4.1 of \cite{itvekbvp}). Now, we have
    \begin{align*}
        &\sup_{0< r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p\,d\theta\\
        &= \sup_{0< r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\frac{1}{k!}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k} \frac{(-1)^{j}}{j!} \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^j (\bar\partial - A)^{k+j}f(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p\,d\theta \\
        &\leq C_{n,p} \sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k}\sup_{0< r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|(\bar\partial - A)^{k+j}f(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p\,d\theta< \infty,
    \end{align*}
    where $C_{n,p}$ is a constant that depends only on $n$ and $p$. Hence, $\varphi_k \in H^p_{A,0}(D)$. 

    Next, suppose that $\varphi_k \in H^p_{A,0}(D)$, for every $k$. Since 
    \[
        (\bar\partial - A)^k f = \sum_{j=k}^{n-1} C_{kj} \widehat{z^*}^{j-k} \varphi_j,
    \]
    for every $0 \leq k \leq n-1$, where $C_{kj}= k!$$ {j}\choose{j-k}$, it follows that 
    \begin{align*}
        &\sup_{0 < r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||(\bar\partial - A)^k f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \\
        &= \sup_{0 < r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\sum_{j=k}^{n-1} C_{kj} \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^{j-k} \varphi_j(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \\
        &\leq C_{n,p} \sum_{j=k}^{n-1} \sup_{0 < r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} \left|\left|\varphi_j(re^{i\theta})\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta < \infty,
    \end{align*}
    where $C_{n,p}$ is a constant that depends on only $n$ and $p$.

title: Theorem
body_md: Let $p$ be a positive real number, $n$ a positive integer, and $A\in W^{n-1,q}(D)$, $q>2$. Every function $w \in V^{n,p}_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ is an element of $L^m(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $0 < m < 2p$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem \ref{Thm: bcmetahardyrep}, every $f \in V^{n,p}_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ is representable as $f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  \widehat{z^*}^k f_k$, where $f_k \in H^p_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$. By Theorem \ref{inBCVekHardypinLebm}, $f_k \in L^m(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $0 < m < 2p$ and every $k$. Hence, we have
 \begin{align*}
    \iint_D ||f(z)||_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy 
    &= \iint_D \left|\left|\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k f_k(z)\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy \\
    &\leq C\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}\iint_D \left|\left|  f_k(z)\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy < \infty,
 \end{align*}
 where $C$ is a constant that depends on $n$ and $m$. Therefore, $f \in L^m(D,\mathbb{B})$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
For $0 < p < \infty$, $n$ a positive integer, and $A \in W^{n-1, q}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q>2$, every $f =\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k \in V^{n,p}_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$ such that $\varphi^+_k \in H^p_{w_k}(D)$, for $w_k \in L^{q_k}(D)$ with $q_k>2$ or $1 < q_k \leq 2$ and $p< \frac{q_k}{2-q_k}$, for every $k$, has a nontangential limit $f_{nt} \in L^p(D, \mathbb{B})$, and 
        \[
            \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta  = 0. 
        \]
head: environment

label: convfork
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $f \in V^{n,p}_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$. By Theorem \ref{Thm: bcmetahardyrep}, 
        \[
            f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k,
        \]
        where $\varphi_k \in H^p_{A,0}(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$. If $\varphi_k^+ \in H^p_{w_k}(D)$, where $w_k \in L^{q_k}(D)$ with $q_k>2$ or $1 < q_k \leq 2$ and $p< \frac{q_k}{2-q_k}$, for every $k$, it follows that $\varphi_{k,nt}$ exists, is in $L^p(\partial D)$, and 
        \begin{equation}\label{convfork}
            \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta  = 0. 
        \end{equation}
        Since $f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  \widehat{z^*}^k \varphi_k$, it follows that 
        \[
            f_{nt} = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_{k,nt}
        \]
        exists, and, for $r \in (0,1)$, we have
        \begin{align*}
            &\int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
            &= \int_0^{2\pi} ||\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
            &\leq C_p \int_0^{2\pi} ||\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
            &\quad\quad + C_p\int_0^{2\pi} ||\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) - \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
            &\leq C_{p,n} \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||  \widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k (\varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \varphi_k(re^{i\theta})) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
            &\quad\quad + C_{p,n} \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi}  ||  (\widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k -  \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k )\varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
            &\leq \widetilde{C_{p,n}} \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||  \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
            &\quad\quad + C_{p,n} \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi}  ||  (\widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k -  \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k )\varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta ,
        \end{align*}
        where $C_{p,n}$ and $\widetilde{C_{p,n}}$ are constants that depend on only $p$ and $n$. Observe that 
        \begin{align*}
            & (\widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k -  \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k )\varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) \\
            &= (e^{-jk\theta} - r^k e^{-jk\theta}) (p^+ \varphi_k^+(re^{i\theta}) + p^- \varphi_k^-(re^{i\theta})) \\
            &= (p^+ e^{ik\theta} + p^- e^{-ik\theta} - r^k (p^+ e^{ik\theta} + p^- e^{-ik\theta})) (p^+ \varphi_k^+(re^{i\theta}) + p^- \varphi_k^-(re^{i\theta})) \\
            &= (p^+ (1-r^k)e^{ik\theta} + p^- (1-r^k)e^{-ik\theta} ) (p^+ \varphi_k^+(re^{i\theta}) + p^- \varphi_k^-(re^{i\theta})) \\
            &= p^+ (1-r^k)e^{ik\theta}\varphi_k^+(re^{i\theta}) + p^- (1-r^k)e^{-ik\theta} \varphi_k^-(re^{i\theta}) .
        \end{align*}

        So, 
        \begin{align*}
&           \widetilde{C_{p,n}} \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi}                ||  \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) -                                   \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
            &\quad\quad + C_{p,n} \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi}  ||  (\widehat{(e^{i\theta})^*}^k -  \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*}^k )\varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta\\
            &= \widetilde{C_{p,n}} \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||  \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
            &\quad\quad + C_{p,n} \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi}  || p^+ (1-r^k)e^{ik\theta}\varphi_k^+(re^{i\theta}) + p^- (1-r^k)e^{-ik\theta} \varphi_k^-(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta\\
            &\leq \widetilde{C_{p,n}} \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||  \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
            &\quad\quad + C_{p,n} 2^{-p/2}\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi}  \left( |(1-r^k)e^{ik\theta}\varphi_k^+(re^{i\theta})| + |(1-r^k)e^{-ik\theta} \varphi_k^-(re^{i\theta}) | \right)^p \, d\theta\\
            &\leq \widetilde{C_{p,n}} \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||  \varphi_{k,nt}(e^{i\theta}) - \varphi_k(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta \\
            &\quad\quad + \widetilde{\widetilde{C_{p,n}}}\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi}  |(1-r^k)|^p\, |\varphi_k^+(re^{i\theta})|^p\,d\theta \\
            &\quad\quad + \widetilde{\widetilde{C_{p,n}}}\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} \int_0^{2\pi} |(1-r^k)|^p \, | \varphi_k^-(re^{i\theta}) |^p  \, d\theta ,
        \end{align*}
        where $C_{p,n}$, $\widetilde{C_{p,n}}$, and $\widetilde{\widetilde{C_{p,n}}}$ are constants that depend on only $p$ and $n$. Observe that, as $r \nearrow 1$, the first sum in the last line of the inequality converges to zero because of (\ref{convfork}), and the second and third sums in the last line of the inequality converge to zero by Lebesgue's Dominated Convergence Theorem. Therefore, 
        \[
            \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta  = 0. 
        \]

label: Thm: bchoivrep
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Thm: bchoivrep}
    For $n$ a positive integer and $A,B \in W^{n-1,q}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q>2$, every $f \in V^{n}_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ has the form 
    \[
        f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^k \varphi_k,
    \]
    where $\varphi_k \in H_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Observe that functions of the form $f(z) = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^k \varphi_k(z)$, where $\varphi_k \in H_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$, are elements of $V^n_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ by direct computation. 

We prove the other direction by induction. The result is clear for $n = 1$. Suppose that, for every $n$ satisfying $1 \leq n \leq m-1$, that if $f \in V^n_{A,B}(D, \mathbb{B})$, then there exists a collection $\{\varphi_k\}_{k=0}^{n-1}$ such that $\varphi_k\in H_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$, and
\[
    f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^k \varphi_k
\]
Let $g \in V^m_{A,B}(D, \mathbb{B})$. So, $(\bar\partial-A-BC(\cdot)) g \in V^{m-1}_{A,B}(D, \mathbb{B})$, and there exists a collection $\{\varphi_k\}_{k=0}^{m-2}$ such that $\varphi_k \in H_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$, and 
\[
    (\bar\partial-A-BC(\cdot)) g = \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^k \varphi_k.
\]
Observe that 
\begin{align*}
    &(\bar\partial-A- BC(\cdot))\left( g - \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}(\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^{k+1} \varphi_k\right) \\  
    &= \left(\bar\partial -A- BC(\cdot)\right)g - (\bar\partial-A- BC(\cdot)) \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}(\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^{k+1} \varphi_k \\
    &= \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^k \varphi_k j- \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^k \varphi_k- \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}(\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^{k+1} (A\varphi_k + BC(\varphi_k)) \\
    &\quad\quad + A \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}(\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^{k+1} \varphi_k + BC(\sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}(\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^{k+1} \varphi_k)\\
    &=- \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}(\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^{k+1} (A\varphi_k + BC(\varphi_k)) \\
    &\quad\quad + \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}(\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^{k+1} A\varphi_k + \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}(\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^{k+1} BC(\varphi_k)\\
    &= 0.
\end{align*}

Thus, $g - \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}(\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^{k+1} \varphi_k \in H_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$. Let 
\[
\gamma = g - \sum_{k=0}^{m-2} \frac{1}{k+1}(\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*}) ^{k+1} \varphi_k.
\]
Let $\phi_0 := \gamma$ and $\phi_{k+1} := \frac{1}{k+1} \varphi_k$, for every $0 \leq k \leq m-2$. Then we rearrange to have
\[
    g = \sum_{j = 0}^{m-1} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^j \phi_j.
\]

label: Thm: bchoivhardyrep
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Thm: bchoivhardyrep}
    For $0 < p < \infty$, $n$ a positive integer, and $A,B \in W^{n-1, q}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q>2$, a function $f$ is in $V^{n,p}_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ with representation 
    \[
        f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^k \varphi_k
    \]
    if and only if $\varphi_k \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First, suppose that $f \in V^{n,p}_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$. By Theorem \ref{Thm: bchoivrep}, 
\[
    f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^k \varphi_k,
\]
where
\[
    \bar\partial\varphi_k = A\varphi_k + B\overline{\varphi_k},
\]
for every $k$. Observe that each $\varphi_k$ is representable as
\[
    \varphi_k = \frac{1}{k!}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k} \frac{(-1)^{j}}{j!} (\widehat{z}+\widehat{z^*})^j (\bar\partial - A-BC(\cdot))^{k+j}f,
\]
    for every $k$. For this formula in the complex setting, see Remark 3.2 of \cite{WBD} (or Theorem 1 of \cite{itvek} or Theorem 4.1 of \cite{itvekbvp}). Using this representation, we can see that, for $r \in (0,1)$, 
\begin{align*}
    &\int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
    &= \int_0^{2\pi} ||\frac{1}{k!}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k} \frac{(-1)^{j}}{j!} (\widehat{re^{i\theta}}+\widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*})^j (\bar\partial - A-BC(\cdot))^{k+j}f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
    &\leq C_{n,k,p} \sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k}  \int_0^{2\pi} ||(\widehat{re^{i\theta}}+\widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*})^j (\bar\partial - A-BC(\cdot))^{k+j}f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
    &\leq C_{n,p} \sum_{j=0}^{n-1-k} ||(\bar\partial - A-BC(\cdot))^{k+j}f(re^{i\theta})||_{H^p}^p <\infty,
\end{align*}
where $C_{n,k,p}$ and $C_{n,p}$ are constants that depend on only $n$, $k$, and $p$. Hence, 
\[
    \sup_{0 < r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta < \infty,
\]
for every $k$, and $\varphi_k \in H^p_{A,B}(D, \mathbb{B})$, for every $k$. 


Now, suppose that $f=\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^k \varphi_k$ solves $(\bar\partial - A - BC(\cdot))^n f = 0$ and $\varphi_k \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $k$. Since 
\[
    (\bar\partial - A- BC(\cdot))^j f = \sum_{k=j}^{n-1} C_{j,n}(\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^{k-j}\varphi_k,
\]
where $C_{j,n}$ is a constant that depends on only $j$ and $k$, for every $0 \leq j \leq n-1$, it follows that, for $r \in (0,1)$, 
\begin{align*}
    &\int_0^{2\pi} ||(\bar\partial - A- BC(\cdot))^j f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta\\
    &= \int_0^{2\pi} ||\sum_{k=j}^{n-1} C_{j,n}(\widehat{re^{i\theta}} + \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*})^{k-j}\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta \\
    &\leq C_{n,p} \sum_{k=j}^{n-1}\int_0^{2\pi}||(\widehat{re^{i\theta}} + \widehat{(re^{i\theta})^*})^{k-j}\varphi_k(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p\\
    &\leq C \sum_{k=j}^{n-1} ||\varphi_k||^{p}_{H^p} < \infty,
\end{align*}
where $C_{n,p}$ and $C$ are constants that depend on only $n$ and $p$. Thus, 
\[
 \sup_{0 < r < 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||(\bar\partial - A- BC(\cdot))^j f(re^{i\theta})||_{\mathbb{B}}^p \,d\theta < \infty,
\]
for every $0 \leq j\leq n-1$, and $f \in V^{n,p}_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$.

body_md: For $0 < p < \infty$, $n$ a positive integer, and $A,B \in W^{n-1, q}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q>2$, every function $f \in V^{n,p}_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ with representation $f = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^k \varphi_k$ such that $\bar\partial \varphi_k \in L^{q_k}(D,\mathbb{B})$, where $q_k>2$ or $1 < q_k \leq 2$ and $p < \frac{q_k}{2 - q_k}$, for every $k$, is in $L^m(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $0 < m < 2p$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem \ref{Thm: bchoivhardyrep}, if $f \in V^{n,p}_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$, then $\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^k f_k$, where every 
    $f_k \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$. Since $f_k \in H^p_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ and $\bar\partial \varphi_k \in L^{q_k}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q_k>2$ or $1 < q_k \leq 2$ and $p < \frac{q_k}{2 - q_k}$, for every $k$, it follows by Theorem \ref{genbcvekhardyinlebm} that $f_k \in L^m(D,\mathbb{B})$, for every $0 < m < 2p$. Thus, 
    \begin{align*}
    \iint_D ||f(z)||_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy 
    &= \iint_D \left|\left|\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1} (\widehat{z} + \widehat{z^*})^k f_k(z)\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy \\
    &\leq C\sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}\iint_D \left|\left|  f_k(z)\right|\right|_{\mathbb{B}}^m \,dx\,dy < \infty,
 \end{align*}
 where $C$ is a constant that depends on $n$ and $m$. Therefore, $f \in L^m(D,\mathbb{B})$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: bchoivhardybvcon}
    For $n$ a positive integer, $0 < p < \infty$, and $A, B \in W^{n-1,q}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q>2$, every $f \in V^{n,p}_{A,B}(D,\mathbb{B})$ with representation $f = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (\widehat{z^*} + \widehat{z})^k \varphi_k$ such that $\varphi_k = h_k + T_\mathbb{B}(A\varphi_k + B\overline{\varphi_k})$, $\bar\partial \varphi_k \in L^{q_k}(D,\mathbb{B})$, $q_k > 2$, and $h_k^+ \in H^p_{\gamma_k}(D)$, $\gamma_k \in L^{\sigma_k}(D)$, $\sigma_k > 2$ or $1 < \sigma_k \leq 2$ and $p < \frac{\sigma_k}{2-\sigma_k}$, for every $k$, has a nontangential boundary value $f_{nt} \in L^p(\partial D,\mathbb{B})$ and 
    \[
        \lim_{r \nearrow 1} \int_0^{2\pi} ||f_{nt}(e^{i\theta}) - f(re^{i\theta}) ||^p_{\mathbb{B}} \, d\theta  = 0. 
    \]
    The result holds for $q_k$ satisfying $1 < q_k \leq 2$ so long as $p$ satisfies $\frac{q_k}{2-q_k}$, for each relevant $k$.
